cards.b: Remove tigers, and deer may boom; remove bees, and crops fall. Ecology studies how living things relate to each other and to their surroundings. It underpins climate policy, farming and conservation.

Organism, population (one species in one place), community (all species), ecosystem (community plus non-living environment: water, soil, light) and biosphere. The word 'ecology' was coined by Ernst Haeckel in 1866; 'ecosystem' by Arthur Tansley in 1935.

Energy enters as sunlight and moves up through producers (plants), herbivores, carnivores and decomposers. Only about 10 percent of energy passes to the next level (Lindeman, 1942), the rest is lost as heat. That is why food chains are short and there are fewer tigers than deer.

Matter recycles; energy does not. Carbon cycle: CO2 taken in by photosynthesis, returned by respiration and burning. Nitrogen cycle: bacteria fix N2 into usable forms; others return it to air. Water cycle: evaporation, rain, runoff. Extra CO2 from fossil fuels is warming Earth.

Populations grow fast at first, then level off at the carrying capacity. Species interact by competition, predation, parasitism, mutualism (bees and flowers) and commensalism. Keystone species, like tigers, wolves and sea otters, have an outsized effect.

Bare rock turns to forest through ecological succession: lichens, mosses, grasses, shrubs, trees. Major biomes are tundra, taiga, temperate forest, grassland, desert, tropical rainforest and aquatic zones. Climate sets the biome.

Threats: habitat loss, invasive species, pollution, over-harvest and climate change (summed up as HIPPO). Conservation is by protected areas (in situ: national parks, reserves) or off-site (ex situ: zoos, seed banks). Edward O. Wilson popularised the term biodiversity.

Tansley (1935) and Lindeman (1942) quantified energy flow. Rachel Carson's Silent Spring (1962) showed pesticide DDT harmed birds. Wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995 and rivers and plants changed (trophic cascade). Keeling's curve has shown CO2 rising since 1958.

Fix these

  • Energy does not cycle; matter does.
  • The top predator is not the 'most important'; every link matters.
  • Climate and weather are different: climate is the long-term pattern.

India has about 100 national parks and over 500 wildlife sanctuaries. Chipko (1973) and the Bishnoi tradition show community conservation. The Biological Diversity Act (2002) and Wildlife (Protection) Act (1972) give legal protection. Silent Valley (Kerala) was saved from a dam in the 1980s. Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove delta. Madhav Gadgil's Western Ghats work shaped debates. India pledged net zero by 2070 at COP26 (2021).

• Energy flows one way; matter cycles.
  • About 10 percent passes up each level.
  • Biodiversity loss is driven mostly by habitat change.
  • Conservation: in situ and ex situ.

Think about it:

  1. Why is a vegetarian diet more energy-efficient?
  2. Why do keystone species matter more than their numbers suggest?
